clue.text: Just taking starters, André Previn has little desire for food

indicators.note: only the opening letters are kept, so 'Just taking starters' picks the first letter of each of the two names

parts.note: petite means small or little

explanation.surface: The conductor André Previn eats only the first courses because he has no hunger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is just a link. 'Just taking starters' gives A and P, the first letters of André and Previn.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a wish to eat is a hunger, the usual meaning of the word.

clue.text: Cliff or Charlie taking Joplin piece, but Douglas rejecting one

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Scott Joplin composed ragtime pieces, each called a rag

explanation.surface: A list of pop singers: Cliff Richard, Charlie, a Scott Joplin rag and Craig Douglas.
explanation.walkthrough: A second route is offered after 'but': the singer Craig Douglas gives CRAIG, which loses I ('one'). Either way the cliff word appears; the parse shows only the first route.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a steep rugged rock face is a cliff.

clue.text: Miles turning round intro for Paul Simon's predecessor?

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters go around another letter
the letters of Miles are turned about into a new order
the intro of a word is its opening letter, here of Paul

explanation.surface: Seems to ask which musician came before Paul Simon, with Miles Davis turning around.
explanation.walkthrough: MILES jumbled ('turning') gives SIMLE, placed 'round' the P that introduces Paul.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme figure is 'Simple Simon', so the word precedes Simon in that name.

clue.text: Sympathy for finishers was flipping wickedness

parts.note: the Rolling Stones song is 'Sympathy for the Devil', so the phrase is completed by that last word

indicators.note: flipping means the two final letters are read in the other direction

parts.note: the finishers (final letters) of Sympathy and for are Y and R

explanation.surface: A Rolling Stones title, with the closing acts turning nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sympathy for' does double duty: it suggests 'the Devil' from the song title, and its last letters Y, R are 'flipping' to give RY.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: devilish behaviour or mischief is wickedness.

clue.text: Dave's partner remixed blue cover for priest

parts.note: Chas and Dave were a British pub-rock duo, so Dave's partner is Chas

indicators.note: a remix rearranges a recording, so the letters of blue are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A musician's bandmate reworks a blues track to cover for a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: BLUE 'remixed' gives UBLE. Chas and Dave were a Cockney singing duo.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless outer vestment worn by a priest saying Mass, so a garment covering him.

clue.text: Crackers in a restaurant?

definitions.meaning: crackers is slang for crazy or not all there
said of someone gone off for a midday meal at an eatery

explanation.surface: Biscuits served in a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for being crazy, and literally describes someone away eating their midday meal.

clue.text: As an older person, poor Ronnie's disheartened

indicators.note: poor signals the remaining letters are knocked into a new arrangement
losing the heart means losing the middle letter, an N

parts.note: the word written as Ronnie's, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Poor old Ronnie feels low as he ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the central N of RONNIES, leaving RONIES, which 'poor' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an elderly person or pensioner is called this.

clue.text: Buddy in Oz with Burl, mostly frolicsome

parts.note: Australians address a mate or pal as 'sport'

indicators.note: mostly means the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Burl Ives was an American folk singer

explanation.surface: Buddy Holly in Australia with Burl Ives, two singers having fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Buddy looks like Buddy Holly, but it is the Australian form of address. 'mostly' cuts IVES to IVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: playful or fond of fun and games.

clue.text: Dance music dynasty

definitions.meaning: a style of electronic club music from 1980s Chicago
a royal family line, such as that of Windsor

explanation.surface: A musical style and a ruling family.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a genre of electronic dance music and also a royal family line.

clue.text: Short bird backing composer

indicators.note: backing means the shortened word is read from the end
short means the word is cut by its final letter

parts.note: the grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: A bird briefly supports a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: GREBE, 'Short', becomes GREB, then 'backing' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School.

clue.text: Tiptoe in as going to pot plant

indicators.note: going to pot means falling to pieces, so these letters are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: Someone creeps in quietly as things fall apart around a potted plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot plant' runs together: 'pot' belongs to the indicator, 'plant' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican plant with red bracts, a common potted Christmas plant.

clue.text: Rice gets British capital for Evita — or The Sound of Music

parts.note: Tim Rice wrote the lyrics for Evita

indicators.note: the capital (initial letter) of Evita

explanation.surface: Tim Rice brings Evita to London, or is it Rodgers and Hammerstein's musical?
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' and 'or The' only join. The surface refers to musicals, but the definition is about the quality of musical sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The distinctive tone quality of a voice or instrument, its characteristic sound.

clue.text: Disturbed soil — not bad clue for Holmes, perhaps

indicators.note: disturbed soil has been moved about, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A detective notices disturbed earth, not a bad clue for Sherlock Holmes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbed soil' reads as the clue Holmes finds, but 'Disturbed' acts on SOIL NOT BAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark of spilt blood is the sort of evidence a fictional detective examines.

clue.text: Coarse jests preceding Long John Silver's last one

indicators.note: preceding places the two letters in front of the singer's surname
last marks the final letter of the word Silver, the pirate's name

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
Long John Baldry was a British blues singer

explanation.surface: Pirate banter preceding Long John Silver's final remark.
explanation.walkthrough: Long John Silver is the pirate of Treasure Island, but the name splits: Long John Baldry the singer, then the final letter of Silver.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: vulgar humour or crude joking.

clue.text: Vinyl binders seen after Queen retrospective

indicators.note: the binding strings are placed after the turned-round royal letters
a retrospective looks back, so the two letters are read backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
cords are strings used to bind things

explanation.surface: Collectors' folders for vinyl at a Queen retrospective exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen looks like the rock band, but is ER, turned by 'retrospective' to RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinyl is used as a collective term for gramophone discs.

clue.text: Female mount is successful

parts.note: a doe is a female deer or rabbit
to mount is to rise or swell

explanation.surface: A female riding a horse succeeds.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to thrive or prosper is to fare successfully.

clue.text: Martin nearly missing odd characters in clergyman's house

parts.note: Dean Martin was an American crooner

indicators.note: dropping the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of nearly leaves the even ones

explanation.surface: Dean Martin almost absent from the vicarage, among some odd characters.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the odd letters of NEARLY leaves ERY.
explanation.definitionFit: The residence of a dean, a senior clergyman.

clue.text: Something falling from artist in ditch

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
the word is used unchanged
to ditch something is to drop it

explanation.surface: An artist tumbles into a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link. Ditch looks like a noun but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A single drop of rain is something that falls from the sky.

clue.text: Music from start to finish for small island

parts.note: rock is a genre of music
the whole of something, all of it

explanation.surface: Music plays all the way through on a tiny island.
explanation.definitionFit: Rockall is an uninhabited islet in the North Atlantic, famous in the shipping forecast.

clue.text: Shaw's good old city

parts.note: Sandie Shaw was the barefoot 1960s pop singer

explanation.surface: George Bernard Shaw's favourite old town.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaw suggests the playwright, but it is singer Sandie Shaw's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A major Californian port, the southernmost large US city on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Noble is tense, saving nothing for later

indicators.note: saving a thing for later means keeping it back until the end
for later says the round letter is kept back to the end of the word

parts.note: the aorist is a past tense of Greek verbs
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An aristocrat grows tense while hoarding nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving ... for later' moves the O of AORIST to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A short informal word for an aristocrat, a member of the nobility.

clue.text: Madonna's first love — musical material

indicators.note: first marks the initial letter of the singer's name

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
Hair is the 1960s rock musical

explanation.surface: Madonna's first love was a musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A fabric made from the hair of the Angora goat.

clue.text: Midnight odyssey starts on boat in capital

indicators.note: starts are the opening letters of Midnight and odyssey

parts.note: a scow is a flat-bottomed boat

explanation.surface: A late-night voyage begins on a boat in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Moscow is the capital city of Russia.

clue.text: Eartha and Orlando trail small birds

parts.note: Eartha Kitt was the American singer
Orlando is the setter, who refers to himself as I
a wake is the trail left behind a ship

explanation.surface: The singer and the setter follow some little birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Orlando is this puzzle's setter, so the name gives I.
explanation.definitionFit: Small gulls of the North Atlantic, named for their call.

clue.text: Funding a musical that may be fascinating?

parts.note: aid is financial help or funding

explanation.surface: Seems to ask whether funding a show could prove fascinating.
explanation.walkthrough: Fascinating Aïda is a British cabaret trio, hence the hint.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Elton John's stage show and Verdi's opera; the comedy group's name supplies the 'fascinating'.

clue.text: King leaves Bilk in tree

indicators.note: the king leaves means that letter departs from the name

parts.note: Acker Bilk was the clarinettist of 'Stranger on the Shore'
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king walks out on a jazz clarinettist sitting in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaves suggests foliage but is the verb of departing.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical name for the maple genus, used for maples generally.

clue.text: Prince shortly goes after bit of tartan fabric

indicators.note: the royal nickname is placed after the opening letter
a bit of tartan is its first letter

parts.note: Prince William, shortened to his nickname

explanation.surface: A prince briefly chases after a scrap of tartan cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong cloth woven with diagonal parallel ribs.

clue.text: Spectator playing no role, OK?

indicators.note: the letters are played around with into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor without a part asks if it is OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone watching rather than taking part, an onlooker.
